e-12401.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration by Changing the Projection Type
e-12401.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/5a19eefe8fdcd63ef9f8a35bf4517b022ab2c35b5fccd06e1e797f67e567653a.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
\iiint\limits_R  f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V
=
\int_0^1\int_{\sqrt{z}}^1\int_0^{y^2-z} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y.$
e-12401.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: \sqrt{z} \leq y \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq x \leq y^2-z \big\}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
\iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V
=
\int_a^b\int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)}\int_{u_1(y,z)}^{u_2(y,z)} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
\iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V
=
\int_a^b\int_{v_1(y)}^{v_2(y)}\int_0^{y^2-z} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/ec195fe4aa1bec5221ec25a1921dfe36e78db34ad3e295fec541c1d05a85d60d.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D = \big\{ (y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq z \leq 1, \:\: \sqrt{z} \leq y \leq 1 \big\}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}z$ to $\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(y),$ is 

$$
y=\sqrt{z}
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
z = y^2
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region is

$$
z=0.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D = \big\{ (y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq z\leq y^2 \big\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/841f014cae7bb224b6f743a86583cb0a70a423d60176b2efd6482d155aa020bc.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\iiint\limits_R f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}V
=

\int_0^1 \int_{0}^{y^2} \int_0^{y^2-z} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y.
$$

e-12403.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration When the Projection Is Partitioned
e-12403.problem:
By changing the order of integration in the following repeated integrals so that they are integrated first with respect to $z,$ then $y,$ and then $x,$ express the following sum as a single repeated integral.

$$
\displaystyle
\int_{-1}^0 \int_{y^2}^{1} \int_{x-1}^{y^2} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y
+
\int_0^1 \int_{y}^{1} \int_{x-1}^{y^2} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y
$$
e-12403.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
\int_a^b \int_{v_1(x)}^{v_2(x)} \int_{u_1(x,y)}^{u_2(x,y)}  f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integrals, we see that the domain of integration $R = R_1\cup R_2,$ where $R_1$ and $R_2$ are type I regions, is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & ={(x,y,z)\,:\,-1\le y\le 0,\,\,{y}^{2}\le x\le 1,\,\,x-1\le z\le {y}^{2}}, \\ {R}_{2} & ={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,y\le x\le 1,\,\,x-1\le z\le {y}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
\int_a^b \int_{v_1(x)}^{v_2(x)} \int_{x-1}^{y^2} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/c8bfd933472e1944f63b1295bda7fc324311ea2ca2ada3636e9f5ab82e4e5fc5.png)

The region $D$ consists of two type II regions in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D =
\left\{ (x,y) \: : \: -1 \leq y \leq 0, \quad y^2 \leq x \leq 1 \right\}
\:\cup\:
\left\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \quad y \leq x \leq 1 \right\}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}x\:\textrm{d}y$ to $\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the lower boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
x=y^2
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
y = -\sqrt{x}
$$

and the upper boundary of the region is

$$
x=y
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
y =x.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region is

$$
D = \left\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \quad -\sqrt{x} \leq y \leq  x \right\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/c73a0e30d6996490f9f41bf3e8777c14d542755387f643ad464bd1dd6cab2839.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\int_0^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{1}} \int_{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{-\sqrt{x}}}^{\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{x}} \int_{x-1}^{y^2} f(x,y,z) \:\textrm{d}z\:\textrm{d}y\:\textrm{d}x.
$$

e-12404.knowledge_point: Evaluating Triple Integrals by Changing the Projection Type
e-12404.problem:
Evaluate
$\displaystyle
\int_{0}^{1} \int_{y}^{1} \int_{0}^{y} 3e^{x^3} \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y.$

*Hint: Change change the order of integration to $\textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x.$*
e-12404.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as 

$$
\int_{a}^{b} \int_{v_1(x)}^{v_2(x)} \int_{u_1(x,y)}^{u_2(x,y)} 3e^{x^3} \:\textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R = \left\{ (x,y,z) \: : \: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \:\: y \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq z \leq y \right\}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
\int_{a}^{b} \int_{v_1(x)}^{v_2(x)} \int_{0}^{y} 3e^{x^3} \:\textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/bdd856ef8a7940a009b7ee27d6614fdb8c042e6655c2316ce4db0633bfd04e9f.png)

The region $D$ is type II region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D = \left\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq y \leq 1, \quad y \leq x \leq 1 \right\}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y$ to $\textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $y = y(x),$ is

$$
x = y \qquad\Longrightarrow \qquad y = x
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region $D$ is

$$
y = 0.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region is

$$
D = \left\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \quad 0 \leq y \leq x \right\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/1e28e1cef9743da80d6fd2d38840810b12239d8546254c4d4cca767568f76a53.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{y}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}3{e}^{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}{\int }_{0}^{y}3{e}^{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}3{e}^{{x}^{3}}[{\int }_{0}^{y}\text{d}z]\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}3{e}^{{x}^{3}}[z]_{0}^{y}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}3y{e}^{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}3{e}^{{x}^{3}}[{\int }_{0}^{x}y\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}3{e}^{{x}^{3}}{[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[{e}^{{x}^{3}}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(e-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to z, then y, and then x.

a

b

decision.explanation: The original bounds describe 0 ≤ x ≤ y ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ z ≤ y² − x². Reversing the order over the xy-projection gives 0 ≤ x ≤ 1 and x ≤ y ≤ 1, while the z-bounds remain unchanged. Thus option b has the required order.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/5907cf8a9103cc9a639fd8078da3646cc0395d28827f58c0f1beef0a1c06645b.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $y,$ and then $x.$
after.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le y,\,\,0\le z\le {y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/a89646433c8851f66c94092b75fae7b46b01f31c69ca03d338464b87bd7f5df4.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le y}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is 

$$
x=y\,⟹\,y=x
$$

and the top boundary of the region is

$$
y=1.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,x\le y\le 1},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/1604e44050208cfb3b4dd81d35bff9769c7498d8304583d5ba92ad4b2f62fd05.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.
$$

Question 1
?

The triple integral of f(x,y,z) over the region R (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫0y∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdxdy

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to z, then y, and then x.

a
 ∫01∫x2x∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
b
 ∫01∫x1∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
c
 ∫01∫0x∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
d
 ∫01∫0x∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
e
 ∫01∫x1∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

From the given repeated integral, we see that R can be written as a type I region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤y≤1,0≤x≤y,0≤z≤y2−x2}

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(x)v2(x)∫u1(x,y)u2(x,y)f(x,y,z)dzdydx

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to z, the z-limits remain the same as before:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(x)v2(x)∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the xy-plane shown below.

The region D is a type II region in the xy-plane:

D={(x,y):0≤y≤1,0≤x≤y}

To change the order of integration from dzdxdy to dzdydx, we write D as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form y=y(x), is

x=y⟹y=x

and the top boundary of the region is

y=1.

Then, the type I representation of the region D is

D={(x,y):0≤x≤1,x≤y≤1},

as shown below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫x1∫0y2−x2f(x,y,z)dzdydx.

content.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration by Changing the Projection Type
content.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/5907cf8a9103cc9a639fd8078da3646cc0395d28827f58c0f1beef0a1c06645b.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $y,$ and then $x.$
content.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le y,\,\,0\le z\le {y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/a89646433c8851f66c94092b75fae7b46b01f31c69ca03d338464b87bd7f5df4.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le y}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is 

$$
x=y\,⟹\,y=x
$$

and the top boundary of the region is

$$
y=1.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,x\le y\le 1},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/1604e44050208cfb3b4dd81d35bff9769c7498d8304583d5ba92ad4b2f62fd05.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.
$$

provenance.kp_title: Swapping the Order of Integration by Changing the Projection Type

history.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le y,\,\,0\le z\le {y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/a89646433c8851f66c94092b75fae7b46b01f31c69ca03d338464b87bd7f5df4.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le y}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is 

$$
x=y\,⟹\,y=x
$$

and the top boundary of the region is

$$
y=1.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,x\le y\le 1},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/1604e44050208cfb3b4dd81d35bff9769c7498d8304583d5ba92ad4b2f62fd05.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.
$$

The triple integral of f(x,y,z) over the region R (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫0x2∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdydx

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to z, then x, and then y.

a
∫01∫0y∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy
b
∫01∫y1∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy
c
∫01∫0y∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy
d
∫01∫y1∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy
e
∫01∫y2y∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy
Submit

decision.explanation: The xy-projection satisfies 0 ≤ x ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ y ≤ x². Since x is nonnegative, reversing these bounds gives 0 ≤ y ≤ 1 and √y ≤ x ≤ 1. The z-bounds remain 0 ≤ z ≤ x² + y, so option d is correct.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/c420d45ca9418fd29889d91a49cce4ae80bb71bdfd4e4aa701b495cc8d87335f.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}+y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $x,$ and then $y.$
after.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le {x}^{2},\,\,0\le z\le {x}^{2}+y}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}+y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/8b7cfa72ed3dbfb121039c6e64b843d83489878a9f457fb1386e455e7d9649ec.png)

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le {x}^{2}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is 

$$
y={x}^{2}\,⟹\,x=\sqrt{y}
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
x=1.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,\sqrt{y}\le x\le 1},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/f49af5da2e4f1f281700e16c4659fabfcd0b15661947ca985d38f208f8563877.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{y}}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}+y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.
$$

Question 2

The triple integral of f(x,y,z) over the region R (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫0x2∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdydx

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to z, then x, and then y.

a
∫01∫0y∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy
b
∫01∫y1∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy
c
∫01∫0y∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy
d
∫01∫y1∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy
e
∫01∫y2y∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

From the given repeated integral, we see that R can be written as a type I region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤x≤1,0≤y≤x2,0≤z≤x2+y}

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫u1(x,y)u2(x,y)f(x,y,z)dzdxdy

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to z, the z-limits remain the same as before:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the xy-plane shown below.

The region D is a type I region in the xy-plane:

D={(x,y):0≤x≤1,0≤y≤x2}

To change the order of integration from dzdydx to dzdxdy, we write D as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form x=x(y), is

y=x2⟹x=y

and the right boundary of the region is

x=1.

Then, the type II representation of the region D is

D={(x,y):0≤y≤1,y≤x≤1},

as shown below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫y1∫0x2+yf(x,y,z)dzdxdy.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option d: reversing 0 ≤ y ≤ x² with 0 ≤ x ≤ 1 gives 0 ≤ y ≤ 1 and √y ≤ x ≤ 1. The z upper bound remains x² + y. The observed incorrect submission was option b, which incorrectly replaces that upper bound with its square root.

content.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration by Changing the Projection Type
content.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/c420d45ca9418fd29889d91a49cce4ae80bb71bdfd4e4aa701b495cc8d87335f.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}+y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $x,$ and then $y.$
content.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le {x}^{2},\,\,0\le z\le {x}^{2}+y}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}+y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/8b7cfa72ed3dbfb121039c6e64b843d83489878a9f457fb1386e455e7d9649ec.png)

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le {x}^{2}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is 

$$
y={x}^{2}\,⟹\,x=\sqrt{y}
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
x=1.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,\sqrt{y}\le x\le 1},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/f49af5da2e4f1f281700e16c4659fabfcd0b15661947ca985d38f208f8563877.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{y}}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}+y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.
$$

decision.explanation: The yz-projection satisfies 0 ≤ z ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ y ≤ ∛z. Equivalently, 0 ≤ y ≤ 1 and y³ ≤ z ≤ 1. The x-bounds remain 1 + y − z ≤ x ≤ 2, giving option a.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/024df0fe0a965feba2177adfac8bbd658fc90f4775a4707f13eba1ef2cb94702.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{z}}{\int }_{1+y-z}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y.$
after.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt[3]{z},\,\,1+y-z\le x\le 2}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{1+y-z}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/8fff232443e6da697862c2e85a9d3abfe0554b80c2fcbfa8c93de42b94a45691.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt[3]{z}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(y),$ is 

$$
y=\sqrt[3]{z}\,⟹\,z={y}^{3}
$$

and the top boundary of the region is

$$
z=1.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,{y}^{3}\le z\le 1},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/726ff420cae25c40f212714141a134fab84633cca7f49bdd268f0668d5248766.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{y}^{3}}^{1}{\int }_{1+y-z}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$

Question 3
?

The triple integral of f(x,y,z) over the region R (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫0z3∫1+y−z2f(x,y,z)dxdydz

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to x, then z, and then y.

a
 ∫01∫y31∫1+y−z2f(x,y,z)dxdzdy
b
 ∫01∫0y3∫1+y−z32f(x,y,z)dxdzdy
c
 ∫01∫11+y∫1+y−z2f(x,y,z)dxdzdy
d
 ∫01∫0y3∫1+y−z2f(x,y,z)dxdzdy
e
 ∫01∫y31∫1+y−z32f(x,y,z)dxdzdy
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

From the given repeated integral, we see that R can be written as a type II region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤z≤1,0≤y≤z3,1+y−z≤x≤2}

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫u1(y,z)u2(y,z)f(x,y,z)dxdzdy

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to x, the x-limits remain the same as before:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫1+y−z2f(x,y,z)dxdzdy

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the yz-plane shown below.

The region D is a type II region in the yz-plane:

D={(y,z):0≤z≤1,0≤y≤z3}

To change the order of integration from dxdydz to dxdzdy, we write D as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form z=z(y), is

y=z3⟹z=y3

and the top boundary of the region is

z=1.

Then, the type I representation of the region D is

D={(y,z):0≤y≤1,y3≤z≤1},

as shown below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫y31∫1+y−z2f(x,y,z)dxdzdy.

content.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration by Changing the Projection Type
content.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/024df0fe0a965feba2177adfac8bbd658fc90f4775a4707f13eba1ef2cb94702.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{z}}{\int }_{1+y-z}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y.$
content.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt[3]{z},\,\,1+y-z\le x\le 2}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{1+y-z}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/8fff232443e6da697862c2e85a9d3abfe0554b80c2fcbfa8c93de42b94a45691.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt[3]{z}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(y),$ is 

$$
y=\sqrt[3]{z}\,⟹\,z={y}^{3}
$$

and the top boundary of the region is

$$
z=1.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,{y}^{3}\le z\le 1},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/726ff420cae25c40f212714141a134fab84633cca7f49bdd268f0668d5248766.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{y}^{3}}^{1}{\int }_{1+y-z}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$

The triple integral of f(x,y,z) over the region R (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫01−y2∫01−x2−y2+1f(x,y,z)dzdxdy

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to z, then y, and then x.

a
 ∫01∫01−x2∫01−x2−y2+1f(x,y,z)dzdydx
b
 ∫01∫01−x2∫0x2+y2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
c
 ∫01∫01−x2∫01−x2−y2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
d
 ∫01∫1x2∫01−x2−y2+1f(x,y,z)dzdydx
e
 ∫01∫1−x21∫0x2+y2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
Submit

decision.explanation: The xy-projection is the quarter disk x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0, x² + y² ≤ 1. Reversing its bounds gives 0 ≤ x ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ y ≤ √(1 − x²). The z-bounds remain 0 ≤ z ≤ √(1 − x² − y²) + 1, so option a is correct.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/c72489a2d33a181fe7bc07d5cc017b93daccac51889cbb61edd64d4ee34429df.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $y,$ and then $x.$
after.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{1-{y}^{2}},\,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}+1}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/98aa4c0a436e4649ccd3d48a53fbf94b0341bf30b95745c4d052381680d223cf.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is 

$$
x=\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}\,⟹\,y=\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region is

$$
y=0.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/47380c108c5b271761de2a027399bbd5981f2a9bdff21e498d73d0b430d070c7.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.
$$

Question 4

The triple integral of f(x,y,z) over the region R (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫01−y2∫01−x2−y2+1f(x,y,z)dzdxdy

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to z, then y, and then x.

a
 ∫01∫01−x2∫01−x2−y2+1f(x,y,z)dzdydx
b
 ∫01∫01−x2∫0x2+y2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
c
 ∫01∫01−x2∫01−x2−y2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
d
 ∫01∫1x2∫01−x2−y2+1f(x,y,z)dzdydx
e
 ∫01∫1−x21∫0x2+y2f(x,y,z)dzdydx
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

From the given repeated integral, we see that R can be written as a type I region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):0≤x≤1,0≤y≤1−y2,0≤z≤1−x2−y2+1}

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(x)v2(x)∫u1(x,y)u2(x,y)f(x,y,z)dzdydx

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to z, the z-limits remain the same as before:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(x)v2(x)∫01−x2−y2+1f(x,y,z)dzdydx

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the xy-plane shown below.

The region D is a type II region in the xy-plane:

D={(x,y):0≤y≤1,0≤x≤1−y2}

To change the order of integration from dzdxdy to dzdydx, we write D as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form y=y(x), is

x=1−y2⟹y=1−x2

and the bottom boundary of the region is

y=0.

Then, the type I representation of the region D is

D={(x,y):0≤x≤1,0≤y≤1−x2},

as shown below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫01∫01−x2∫01−x2−y2+1f(x,y,z)dzdydx.

verification.explanation: Option a matches the original quarter-disk projection: 0 ≤ x ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ y ≤ √(1 − x²), with the z-bounds unchanged. The worked solution’s final integral confirms this; its initial region description contains a typo. The observed incorrect submission was option e, not a.

content.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration by Changing the Projection Type
content.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/c72489a2d33a181fe7bc07d5cc017b93daccac51889cbb61edd64d4ee34429df.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $y,$ and then $x.$
content.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{1-{y}^{2}},\,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}+1}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/98aa4c0a436e4649ccd3d48a53fbf94b0341bf30b95745c4d052381680d223cf.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is 

$$
x=\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}\,⟹\,y=\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region is

$$
y=0.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/47380c108c5b271761de2a027399bbd5981f2a9bdff21e498d73d0b430d070c7.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.
$$

The triple integral of f(x,y,z) over the region R (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫14∫−4/x−1∫02+xy/2f(x,y,z)dzdydx

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to z, then x, and then y.

a
 ∫−4−1∫1−4/y∫04/(xy)f(x,y,z)dzdxdy
b
 ∫−4−1∫0−4/y∫02+xy/2f(x,y,z)dzdxdy
c
 ∫−4−1∫−4/y4∫04/(xy)f(x,y,z)dzdxdy
d
 ∫−4−1∫−4/y4∫02+xy/2f(x,y,z)dzdxdy
e
 ∫−4−1∫1−4/y∫02+xy/2f(x,y,z)dzdxdy

decision.explanation: The projection satisfies 1 ≤ x ≤ 4 and −4/x ≤ y ≤ −1. Thus −4 ≤ y ≤ −1; multiplying y ≥ −4/x by x > 0 and dividing by y < 0 gives x ≤ −4/y. Therefore 1 ≤ x ≤ −4/y, with the z-bounds unchanged, yielding option e.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/fcc776a63cd1ac9fc5ec91157652ce9e75c6ee515eca8c6223309521cc300b61.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{-4/x}^{-1}{\int }_{0}^{2+xy/2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $x,$ and then $y.$
after.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,1\le x\le 4,\,\,-\frac{4}{x}\le y\le -1,\,\,0\le z\le 2+\frac{xy}{2}}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{0}^{2+xy/2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/1f30c28c7c048faae864da08a5a6d67d0c6346b27c00a9e7726234531f2f0783.png)

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 4,\,\,-\frac{4}{x}\le y\le -1}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the right boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is 

$$
y=-\frac{4}{x}\,⟹\,x=-\frac{4}{y}
$$

and the left boundary of the region is

$$
x=1.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-4\le y\le -1,\,\,1\le x\le -\frac{4}{y}},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/acc210f36bccb873526172149b85941bd42bc1648a464862562723fedca27bcb.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{-4}^{-1}{\int }_{1}^{-4/y}{\int }_{0}^{2+xy/2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.
$$

Question 5
?

The triple integral of f(x,y,z) over the region R (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫14∫−4/x−1∫02+xy/2f(x,y,z)dzdydx

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to z, then x, and then y.

a
 ∫−4−1∫1−4/y∫04/(xy)f(x,y,z)dzdxdy
b
 ∫−4−1∫0−4/y∫02+xy/2f(x,y,z)dzdxdy
c
 ∫−4−1∫−4/y4∫04/(xy)f(x,y,z)dzdxdy
d
 ∫−4−1∫−4/y4∫02+xy/2f(x,y,z)dzdxdy
e
 ∫−4−1∫1−4/y∫02+xy/2f(x,y,z)dzdxdy
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

From the given repeated integral, we see that R can be written as a type I region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):1≤x≤4,−4x≤y≤−1,0≤z≤2+xy2}

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫u1(x,y)u2(x,y)f(x,y,z)dzdxdy

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to z, the z-limits remain the same as before:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫02+xy/2f(x,y,z)dzdxdy

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the xy-plane shown below.

The region D is a type I region in the xy-plane:

D={(x,y):1≤x≤4,−4x≤y≤−1}

To change the order of integration from dzdydx to dzdxdy, we write D as a type II region.

Notice that the right boundary of the region, written in the form x=x(y), is

y=−4x⟹x=−4y

and the left boundary of the region is

x=1.

Then, the type II representation of the region D is

D={(x,y):−4≤y≤−1,1≤x≤−4y},

as shown below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫−4−1∫1−4/y∫02+xy/2f(x,y,z)dzdxdy.

content.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration by Changing the Projection Type
content.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/fcc776a63cd1ac9fc5ec91157652ce9e75c6ee515eca8c6223309521cc300b61.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{-4/x}^{-1}{\int }_{0}^{2+xy/2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $x,$ and then $y.$
content.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,1\le x\le 4,\,\,-\frac{4}{x}\le y\le -1,\,\,0\le z\le 2+\frac{xy}{2}}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{0}^{2+xy/2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/1f30c28c7c048faae864da08a5a6d67d0c6346b27c00a9e7726234531f2f0783.png)

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 4,\,\,-\frac{4}{x}\le y\le -1}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the right boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is 

$$
y=-\frac{4}{x}\,⟹\,x=-\frac{4}{y}
$$

and the left boundary of the region is

$$
x=1.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-4\le y\le -1,\,\,1\le x\le -\frac{4}{y}},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/acc210f36bccb873526172149b85941bd42bc1648a464862562723fedca27bcb.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{-4}^{-1}{\int }_{1}^{-4/y}{\int }_{0}^{2+xy/2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.
$$

∫−11∫y3−2y∫y/2x+4dzdxdy=∫−3p∫−1q∫y/2x+4dzdydx+∫−11∫r1∫y/2x+4dzdydx

a
p=−1,q=(x+2)3,r=x
b
 p=−1,q=x+23,r=x

decision.explanation: The projection satisfies −1 ≤ y ≤ 1, y ≥ x, and y ≤ (x+2)³. For −3 ≤ x ≤ −1, the y-bounds are −1 to (x+2)³. For −1 ≤ x ≤ 1, they are x to 1. Hence p = −1, q = (x+2)³, and r = x.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
By changing the order of integration, find the missing limits in the following repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt[3]{y}-2}^{y}{\int }_{y/2}^{x+4}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y={\int }_{-3}^{p}{\int }_{-1}^{q}{\int }_{y/2}^{x+4}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{r}^{1}{\int }_{y/2}^{x+4}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$
after.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(y)}^{{v}_{4}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{3}(x,y)}^{{u}_{4}(x,y)}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,-1\le y\le 1,\,\,\sqrt[3]{y}-2\le x\le y,\,\,\frac{y}{2}\le z\le x+4}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt[3]{y}-2}^{y}{\int }_{y/2}^{x+4}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{y/2}^{x+4}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(x)}^{{v}_{4}(x)}{\int }_{y/2}^{x+4}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/c92ab09dc71043ac3f5265202f36e38110e5e8db9f2dd115ab006721ed66d4c0.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le y\le 1,\,\sqrt[3]{y}-2\le x\le y}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x,$ we split $D$ into two type I regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/8ac0e7631d0baa8ba3b4c37ebe2b2b1d8efa650495d197f425aba093f342a9d3.png)

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the left region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ are

$\,$ $y=-1\,$ and $\,y=(x+2)^{3}.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the right region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ are

$\,$ $y=x\,$ and $\,y=1.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,-3\le x\le -1,\,-1\le y\le (x+2)^{3}}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 1,\,x\le y\le 1}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{-1}{\int }_{-1}^{(x+2)^{3}}{\int }_{y/2}^{x+4}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1}{\int }_{y/2}^{x+4}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

after.html:
Question 6
?

By changing the order of integration, find the missing limits in the following repeated integral.

∫−11∫y3−2y∫y/2x+4dzdxdy=∫−3p∫−1q∫y/2x+4dzdydx+∫−11∫r1∫y/2x+4dzdydx

a
p=−1,q=(x+2)3,r=x
b
 p=−1,q=x+23,r=x
c
 p=−2,q=3(x+2),r=−x
d
 p=−1,q=(x+2)3,r=x2
e
 p=−2,q=x+23,r=−x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as ∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫u1(x,y)u2(x,y)dzdydx+∫cd∫v3(y)v4(y)∫u3(x,y)u4(x,y)dzdydx.

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration R can be written as a type I region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):−1≤y≤1,y3−2≤x≤y,y2≤z≤x+4}

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to z, the z-limits remain the same as before:

∫−11∫y3−2y∫y/2x+4dzdxdy=∫ab∫v1(x)v2(x)∫y/2x+4dzdydx+∫cd∫v3(x)v4(x)∫y/2x+4dzdydx

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the xy-plane shown below.

The region D is a type II region in the xy-plane:

D={(x,y):−1≤y≤1,y3−2≤x≤y}.

To change the order of integration from dzdxdy to dzdydx, we split D into two type I regions.

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the left region, written in the form y=y(x), are

y=−1 and y=(x+2)3.

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the right region, written in the form y=y(x), are

y=x and y=1.

So, we can write D as a union of

D1={(x,y):−3≤x≤−1,−1≤y≤(x+2)3}

and

D2={(x,y):−1≤x≤1,x≤y≤1}.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

∫−3−1∫−1(x+2)3∫y/2x+4dzdydx+∫−11∫x1∫y/2x+4dzdydx.

content.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration When the Projection Is Partitioned
content.problem:
By changing the order of integration, find the missing limits in the following repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt[3]{y}-2}^{y}{\int }_{y/2}^{x+4}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y={\int }_{-3}^{p}{\int }_{-1}^{q}{\int }_{y/2}^{x+4}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{r}^{1}{\int }_{y/2}^{x+4}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$
content.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(y)}^{{v}_{4}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{3}(x,y)}^{{u}_{4}(x,y)}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,-1\le y\le 1,\,\,\sqrt[3]{y}-2\le x\le y,\,\,\frac{y}{2}\le z\le x+4}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt[3]{y}-2}^{y}{\int }_{y/2}^{x+4}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{y/2}^{x+4}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(x)}^{{v}_{4}(x)}{\int }_{y/2}^{x+4}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/c92ab09dc71043ac3f5265202f36e38110e5e8db9f2dd115ab006721ed66d4c0.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $xy$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le y\le 1,\,\sqrt[3]{y}-2\le x\le y}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x,$ we split $D$ into two type I regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/8ac0e7631d0baa8ba3b4c37ebe2b2b1d8efa650495d197f425aba093f342a9d3.png)

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the left region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ are

$\,$ $y=-1\,$ and $\,y=(x+2)^{3}.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the right region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ are

$\,$ $y=x\,$ and $\,y=1.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,-3\le x\le -1,\,-1\le y\le (x+2)^{3}}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 1,\,x\le y\le 1}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{-1}{\int }_{-1}^{(x+2)^{3}}{\int }_{y/2}^{x+4}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{x}^{1}{\int }_{y/2}^{x+4}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

decision.explanation: The yz-projection gives −1 ≤ z ≤ 2 and 0 ≤ y ≤ min(2, (z+1)²/2, 4−2z). The upper boundary changes at z=1: it is (z+1)²/2 for −1 ≤ z ≤ 1 and 4−2z for 1 ≤ z ≤ 2. Thus p=1, q=2, and r=4−2z.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
By changing the order of integration, find the missing limits in the following repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{\sqrt{2y}-1}^{2-y/2}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y={\int }_{-1}^{p}{\int }_{0}^{(z+1)^{2}/2}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{1}^{q}{\int }_{0}^{r}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$
after.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(z)}^{{v}_{4}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{3}(xy,z)}^{{u}_{4}(y,z)}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,\sqrt{2y}-1\le z\le 2-\frac{y}{2},\,\,-2z\le x\le y+3}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{\sqrt{2y}-1}^{2-y/2}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(z)}^{{v}_{4}(x)}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/a4de9d9df51efcec67253a1c7118466f29459ffd5c9136c144d33500ec5557bc.png)

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\sqrt{2y}-1\le z\le 2-\frac{y}{2}}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z,$ we split $D$ into two type II regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/18bb3e55f076e022176bb60df27d5665ed2d91d75d618969c04ce192378db922.png)

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the lower region, written in the form $y=y(z),$ are

$\,$ $y=0\,$ and $\,y=\frac{1}{2}(z+1)^{2}.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the upper region, written in the form $y=y(z),$ are

$\,$ $y=0\,$ and $\,y=4-2z.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}={(y,z)\,:\,-1\le z\le 1,\,0\le y\le \frac{1}{2}(z+1)^{2}}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}={(y,z)\,:\,1\le z\le 2,\,0\le x\le 4-2z}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$

$$

content.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration When the Projection Is Partitioned
content.problem:
By changing the order of integration, find the missing limits in the following repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{\sqrt{2y}-1}^{2-y/2}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y={\int }_{-1}^{p}{\int }_{0}^{(z+1)^{2}/2}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{1}^{q}{\int }_{0}^{r}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$
content.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(z)}^{{v}_{4}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{3}(xy,z)}^{{u}_{4}(y,z)}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,\sqrt{2y}-1\le z\le 2-\frac{y}{2},\,\,-2z\le x\le y+3}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{\sqrt{2y}-1}^{2-y/2}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(z)}^{{v}_{4}(x)}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/a4de9d9df51efcec67253a1c7118466f29459ffd5c9136c144d33500ec5557bc.png)

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\sqrt{2y}-1\le z\le 2-\frac{y}{2}}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z,$ we split $D$ into two type II regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/18bb3e55f076e022176bb60df27d5665ed2d91d75d618969c04ce192378db922.png)

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the lower region, written in the form $y=y(z),$ are

$\,$ $y=0\,$ and $\,y=\frac{1}{2}(z+1)^{2}.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the upper region, written in the form $y=y(z),$ are

$\,$ $y=0\,$ and $\,y=4-2z.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}={(y,z)\,:\,-1\le z\le 1,\,0\le y\le \frac{1}{2}(z+1)^{2}}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}={(y,z)\,:\,1\le z\le 2,\,0\le x\le 4-2z}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{(z+1)^{2}/2}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{4-2z}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.\end{aligned}
$$

{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(z)}^{{v}_{4}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{3}(xy,z)}^{{u}_{4}(y,z)}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,\sqrt{2y}-1\le z\le 2-\frac{y}{2},\,\,-2z\le x\le y+3}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{\sqrt{2y}-1}^{2-y/2}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(z)}^{{v}_{4}(x)}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/a4de9d9df51efcec67253a1c7118466f29459ffd5c9136c144d33500ec5557bc.png)

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\sqrt{2y}-1\le z\le 2-\frac{y}{2}}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z,$ we split $D$ into two type II regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/18bb3e55f076e022176bb60df27d5665ed2d91d75d618969c04ce192378db922.png)

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the lower region, written in the form $y=y(z),$ are

$\,$ $y=0\,$ and $\,y=\frac{1}{2}(z+1)^{2}.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the upper region, written in the form $y=y(z),$ are

$\,$ $y=0\,$ and $\,y=4-2z.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}={(y,z)\,:\,-1\le z\le 1,\,0\le y\le \frac{1}{2}(z+1)^{2}}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}={(y,z)\,:\,1\le z\le 2,\,0\le x\le 4-2z}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{(z+1)^{2}/2}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{4-2z}{\int }_{-2z}^{y+3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8
?

By changing the order of integration, find the missing limits in the following repeated integral.

∫−20∫(x2−4)/2(x+2)3/4∫xy2dzdydx=∫p0∫q0∫xy2dzdxdy+∫02∫r0∫xy2dzdxdy

a
 p=−1,q=y+1,r=y3
b
 p=−2,q=−2y+4,r=y3
c
 p=−2,q=−2y+1,r=2y3−1
d
 p=−2,q=−2y+4,r=4y3−2
e
 p=−1,q=y+1,r=4y3−2
Submit

decision.explanation: The y-range is −2 to 2, split at y=0. For −2 ≤ y ≤ 0, y ≥ (x²−4)/2 gives −√(2y+4) ≤ x ≤ 0. For 0 ≤ y ≤ 2, y ≤ (x+2)³/4 gives ∛(4y)−2 ≤ x ≤ 0. Thus option d supplies all three limits.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
By changing the order of integration, find the missing limits in the following repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{({x}^{2}-4)/2}^{(x+2)^{3}/4}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={\int }_{p}^{0}{\int }_{q}^{0}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{r}^{0}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$
after.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(y)}^{{v}_{4}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{3}(x,y)}^{{u}_{4}(x,y)}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,-2\le x\le 0,\,\,\frac{1}{2}({x}^{2}-4)\le y\le \frac{1}{4}(x+2)^{3},\,\,x\le z\le {y}^{2}}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{({x}^{2}-4)/2}^{(x+2)^{3}/4}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(y)}^{{v}_{4}(y)}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/a38afc63496b487803590ccd57e2ab92ad4061524007e8bb4fb6277ff952dde2.png)

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $xz$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 0,\,\frac{1}{2}({x}^{2}-4)\le y\le \frac{1}{4}(x+2)^{3}}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y,$ we split $D$ into two type II regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/9bbaf6d9ce11ecbd988954365e9693f7f3f175c1dd0f944cc85b73773beca047.png)

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the lower region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ are

$\,$ $x=-\sqrt{2y+4}\,$ and $\,x=0.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the upper region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ are

$\,$ $x=\sqrt[3]{4y}-2\,$ and $\,x=0.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le y\le 0,\,-\sqrt{2y+4}\le x\le 0}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\sqrt[3]{4y}-2\le x\le 0}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{-\sqrt{2y+4}}^{0}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{\sqrt[3]{4y}-2}^{0}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8
?

By changing the order of integration, find the missing limits in the following repeated integral.

∫−20∫(x2−4)/2(x+2)3/4∫xy2dzdydx=∫p0∫q0∫xy2dzdxdy+∫02∫r0∫xy2dzdxdy

a
 p=−1,q=y+1,r=y3
b
 p=−2,q=−2y+4,r=y3
c
 p=−2,q=−2y+1,r=2y3−1
d
 p=−2,q=−2y+4,r=4y3−2
e
 p=−1,q=y+1,r=4y3−2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as ∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫u1(x,y)u2(x,y)dzdxdy+∫cd∫v3(y)v4(y)∫u3(x,y)u4(x,y)dzdxdy.

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration R can be written as a type I region as follows:

R={(x,y,z):−2≤x≤0,12(x2−4)≤y≤14(x+2)3,x≤z≤y2}

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to z, the z-limits remain the same as before:

∫−20∫(x2−4)/2(x+2)3/4∫xy2dzdydx=∫ab∫v1(y)v2(y)∫xy2dzdxdy+∫cd∫v3(y)v4(y)∫xy2dzdxdy

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the xy-plane shown below.

The region D is a type I region in the xz-plane:

D={(x,y):−2≤x≤0,12(x2−4)≤y≤14(x+2)3}.

To change the order of integration from dzdydx to dzdxdy, we split D into two type II regions.

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the lower region, written in the form x=x(y), are

x=−2y+4 and x=0.

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the upper region, written in the form x=x(y), are

x=4y3−2 and x=0.

So, we can write D as a union of

D1={(x,y):−2≤y≤0,−2y+4≤x≤0}

and

D2={(x,y):0≤y≤2,4y3−2≤x≤0}.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

∫−20∫−2y+40∫xy2dzdxdy+∫02∫4y3−20∫xy2dzdxdy.

content.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration When the Projection Is Partitioned
content.problem:
By changing the order of integration, find the missing limits in the following repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{({x}^{2}-4)/2}^{(x+2)^{3}/4}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={\int }_{p}^{0}{\int }_{q}^{0}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{r}^{0}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$
content.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(y)}^{{v}_{4}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{3}(x,y)}^{{u}_{4}(x,y)}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,-2\le x\le 0,\,\,\frac{1}{2}({x}^{2}-4)\le y\le \frac{1}{4}(x+2)^{3},\,\,x\le z\le {y}^{2}}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{({x}^{2}-4)/2}^{(x+2)^{3}/4}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(y)}^{{v}_{4}(y)}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/a38afc63496b487803590ccd57e2ab92ad4061524007e8bb4fb6277ff952dde2.png)

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $xz$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 0,\,\frac{1}{2}({x}^{2}-4)\le y\le \frac{1}{4}(x+2)^{3}}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y,$ we split $D$ into two type II regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/9bbaf6d9ce11ecbd988954365e9693f7f3f175c1dd0f944cc85b73773beca047.png)

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the lower region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ are

$\,$ $x=-\sqrt{2y+4}\,$ and $\,x=0.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the upper region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ are

$\,$ $x=\sqrt[3]{4y}-2\,$ and $\,x=0.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le y\le 0,\,-\sqrt{2y+4}\le x\le 0}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\sqrt[3]{4y}-2\le x\le 0}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{-\sqrt{2y+4}}^{0}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{\sqrt[3]{4y}-2}^{0}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,y)}^{{u}_{2}(x,y)}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(y)}^{{v}_{4}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{3}(x,y)}^{{u}_{4}(x,y)}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,-2\le x\le 0,\,\,\frac{1}{2}({x}^{2}-4)\le y\le \frac{1}{4}(x+2)^{3},\,\,x\le z\le {y}^{2}}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $z,$ the $z$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{({x}^{2}-4)/2}^{(x+2)^{3}/4}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(y)}^{{v}_{4}(y)}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/a38afc63496b487803590ccd57e2ab92ad4061524007e8bb4fb6277ff952dde2.png)

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $xz$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 0,\,\frac{1}{2}({x}^{2}-4)\le y\le \frac{1}{4}(x+2)^{3}}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y,$ we split $D$ into two type II regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/9bbaf6d9ce11ecbd988954365e9693f7f3f175c1dd0f944cc85b73773beca047.png)

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the lower region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ are

$\,$ $x=-\sqrt{2y+4}\,$ and $\,x=0.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the upper region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ are

$\,$ $x=\sqrt[3]{4y}-2\,$ and $\,x=0.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le y\le 0,\,-\sqrt{2y+4}\le x\le 0}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\sqrt[3]{4y}-2\le x\le 0}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{-\sqrt{2y+4}}^{0}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{\sqrt[3]{4y}-2}^{0}{\int }_{x}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 9
?

By changing the order of integration in the following repeated integrals so that they are integrated first with respect to x, then y, and then z, express the following sum as a single repeated integral.

∫−22∫0y+2∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdzdy+∫26∫06−y∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdzdy

a
 ∫04∫z26−z2∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdydz
b
 ∫04∫z2+16−z∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdydz
c
 ∫02∫2z26+z2∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdydz
d
 ∫02∫z−26−z∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdydz
e
 ∫02∫z2−26−z2∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdydz
Submit

decision.explanation: Reversing the yz-projection gives z²−2 ≤ y ≤ 2 from the first integral and 2 ≤ y ≤ 6−z² from the second. Their union is z²−2 ≤ y ≤ 6−z² for 0 ≤ z ≤ 2. The x-bounds remain −z to y², so option e is correct.

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
By changing the order of integration in the following repeated integrals so that they are integrated first with respect to $x,$ then $y,$ and then $z,$ express the following sum as a single repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{y+2}}{\int }_{-z}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{2}^{6}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{6-y}}{\int }_{-z}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$
after.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.
$$

From the repeated integrals, we see that the domain of integration $R={R}_{1}\cup {R}_{2},$ where ${R}_{1}$ and ${R}_{2}$ are type I regions, is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & ={(x,y,z)\,:\,-2\le y\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{y+2},\,\,-z\le x\le {y}^{2}}, \\ {R}_{2} & ={(x,y,z)\,:\,2\le y\le 6,\,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{6-y},\,\,-z\le x\le {y}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{-z}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/aa1c884900c3cb01a719dc6d22604469984d2b08291d9d925b8f37d794d455b2.png)

The region $D$ consists of two type I regions in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,-2\le y\le 2,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{y+2}}\,\cup \,{(y,z)\,:\,2\le x\le 6,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{6-y}}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(z),$ is

$$
z=\sqrt{y+2}\,⟹\,y={z}^{2}-2
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
z=\sqrt{6-y}\,⟹\,y=6-{z}^{2}.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region is

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 2,\,{z}^{2}-2\le y\le 6-{z}^{2}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/e4139dde4d56e83b91e4a72d42ccdf296ad20773520ccdaa51d7a84b9e1a3f31.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-2}^{6-{z}^{2}}{\int }_{-z}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.
$$

Question 9

By changing the order of integration in the following repeated integrals so that they are integrated first with respect to x, then y, and then z, express the following sum as a single repeated integral.

∫−22∫0y+2∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdzdy+∫26∫06−y∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdzdy

a
 ∫04∫z26−z2∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdydz
b
 ∫04∫z2+16−z∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdydz
c
 ∫02∫2z26+z2∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdydz
d
 ∫02∫z−26−z∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdydz
e
 ∫02∫z2−26−z2∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdydz
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as ∫ab∫v1(z)v2(z)∫u1(y,z)u2(y,z)f(x,y,z)dxdydz.

From the repeated integrals, we see that the domain of integration R=R1∪R2, where R1 and R2 are type I regions, is given by

R1={(x,y,z):−2≤y≤2,0≤z≤y+2,−z≤x≤y2},R2={(x,y,z):2≤y≤6,0≤z≤6−y,−z≤x≤y2}.

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to x, the x-limits remain the same as before:

∫ab∫v1(z)v2(z)∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdydz

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the yz-plane shown below.

The region D consists of two type I regions in the yz-plane:

D={(y,z):−2≤y≤2,0≤z≤y+2}∪{(y,z):2≤x≤6,0≤z≤6−y}.

To change the order of integration from dxdzdy to dxdydz, we write D as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form y=y(z), is z=y+2⟹y=z2−2 and the right boundary of the region is z=6−y⟹y=6−z2.

Then, the type II representation of the region is

D={(y,z):0≤z≤2,z2−2≤y≤6−z2},

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

∫02∫z2−26−z2∫−zy2f(x,y,z)dxdydz.

content.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration When the Projection Is Partitioned
content.problem:
By changing the order of integration in the following repeated integrals so that they are integrated first with respect to $x,$ then $y,$ and then $z,$ express the following sum as a single repeated integral.

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{y+2}}{\int }_{-z}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{2}^{6}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{6-y}}{\int }_{-z}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$
content.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.
$$

From the repeated integrals, we see that the domain of integration $R={R}_{1}\cup {R}_{2},$ where ${R}_{1}$ and ${R}_{2}$ are type I regions, is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & ={(x,y,z)\,:\,-2\le y\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{y+2},\,\,-z\le x\le {y}^{2}}, \\ {R}_{2} & ={(x,y,z)\,:\,2\le y\le 6,\,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{6-y},\,\,-z\le x\le {y}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{-z}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/aa1c884900c3cb01a719dc6d22604469984d2b08291d9d925b8f37d794d455b2.png)

The region $D$ consists of two type I regions in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,-2\le y\le 2,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{y+2}}\,\cup \,{(y,z)\,:\,2\le x\le 6,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{6-y}}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(z),$ is

$$
z=\sqrt{y+2}\,⟹\,y={z}^{2}-2
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
z=\sqrt{6-y}\,⟹\,y=6-{z}^{2}.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region is

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 2,\,{z}^{2}-2\le y\le 6-{z}^{2}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/e4139dde4d56e83b91e4a72d42ccdf296ad20773520ccdaa51d7a84b9e1a3f31.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-2}^{6-{z}^{2}}{\int }_{-z}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.
$$

D={(y,z)\,:\,-2\le y\le 2,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{y+2}}\,\cup \,{(y,z)\,:\,2\le x\le 6,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{6-y}}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(z),$ is

$$
z=\sqrt{y+2}\,⟹\,y={z}^{2}-2
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
z=\sqrt{6-y}\,⟹\,y=6-{z}^{2}.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region is

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 2,\,{z}^{2}-2\le y\le 6-{z}^{2}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/e4139dde4d56e83b91e4a72d42ccdf296ad20773520ccdaa51d7a84b9e1a3f31.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{z}^{2}-2}^{6-{z}^{2}}{\int }_{-z}^{{y}^{2}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.
$$
